To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of duplicated genes created by large-scale duplications is less divergent than that of duplicated genes created through small-scale duplications, and that this is strongly influenced by the function of the gene and the biological process it is involved in.
gene expression is highly correlated for genes created by large-scale duplications and that this correlation decreases over time.
the expression divergence of duplicated genes is strongly dependent on the origin and function of the duplicated gene and that the divergence is asymmetric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of duplicated genes and shows that the expression divergence of duplicated genes is strongly influenced by the mode of duplication and the functional class of the gene involved.
how duplicated genes diverge from each other and how they evolve after duplication.
the fate of genes following duplication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the divergence of gene function after duplication is not random, but depends on the mode of duplication and on the function and biological process of the duplicated genes.

the expression of genes that were duplicated by large-scale duplication and that can still found in duplicated segments is more conserved than that of genes that were generated by small-scale duplication or that have lost their duplicates.
the mode of gene duplication, the function, and the time after duplication all influence the expression divergence of gene duplicates in A. thaliana.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gene expression divergence is a nonrandom process that is strongly influenced by the mode of duplication and gene function.
the mode of gene duplication and gene function are important determinants in the divergence of expression of duplicated genes.
the mode of gene duplication and the function of duplicated genes have a strong impact on the divergence in expression and, therefore on the evolution of the function of genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the divergence of gene function and gene expression after duplication is nonrandom.
the functional divergence of duplicated genes can be predicted from the expression divergence of these genes.
gene expression is not only important for the maintenance of gene function but also plays a role in the fate of duplicated genes after duplication.
